device.model: niryo_moveit MoverService (MoveIt) of the Unity Robotics Hub pick-and-place tutorial
device.name: Niryo pick-and-place planner (Unity Robotics Hub)

facts.text: moveit_server initialises moveit_commander, starts node niryo_moveit_server, advertises service niryo_moveit of type MoverService with callback plan_pick_and_place, and calls rospy.spin.
MoverService takes NiryoMoveitJoints joints_input, a geometry_msgs/Pose pick_pose and a geometry_msgs/Pose place_pose, and returns a moveit_msgs/RobotTrajectory[] named trajectories.
NiryoMoveitJoints carries float64[6] joints and its own geometry_msgs/Pose pick_pose and place_pose.
moveit_msgs/RobotTrajectory holds a trajectory_msgs/JointTrajectory joint_trajectory and a trajectory_msgs/MultiDOFJointTrajectory multi_dof_joint_trajectory.
The moveit_msgs package version is 0.11.1 and its license element is BSD.
The planner's joint names are joint_1, joint_2, joint_3, joint_4, joint_5 and joint_6.

plan_trajectory writes the given start angles into a JointState, sets that as the MoveIt start state, sets the destination pose, calls move_group.plan, raises Exception when the plan is false, and otherwise returns planCompat(plan).
planCompat returns plan[1] when sys.version_info is at least (3, 0), and otherwise returns plan.
plan_pick_and_place constructs a MoveGroupCommander for the group name arm as a local variable.
The start configuration is req.joints_input.joints.
The pre-grasp plan targets req.pick_pose from that start configuration.
When the pre-grasp trajectory has no points, plan_pick_and_place returns the still-empty response.
The grasp plan targets a copy of req.pick_pose whose position.z is reduced by 0.05; the comment calls that a static value coming from Unity.
When the grasp trajectory has no points, the callback returns the still-empty response.
The pick-up plan targets req.pick_pose from the grasp plan's last joint positions.
When the pick-up trajectory has no points, the callback returns the still-empty response.
The place plan targets req.place_pose.
When the place trajectory has no points, the callback returns the still-empty response.
When every stage has points, the callback appends the four plans and calls clear_pose_targets.
The docstring says gripper behaviour is handled outside this trajectory planning.
The SRDF group arm is the chain from base_link to tool_link.
The SRDF file header says the program is free software under the GNU General Public License, either version 3 or any later version.
part_3.launch starts server_endpoint from ros_tcp_endpoint, the mover node running mover.py, and includes demo.launch. The tcp_port argument defaults to 10000.
demo.launch includes controllers.launch with simulation_mode true and includes move_group.launch.
controllers.launch defaults simulation_mode to false. Its comment says true makes the controller echo the position command and deactivates hardware. fake_communication is set from simulation_mode.
controllers.launch spawns joint_state_controller and niryo_one_follow_joint_trajectory_controller.
move_group.launch defaults allow_trajectory_execution to true and fake_execution to false.
demo.launch sets /move_group/start_state_max_bounds_error to 0.3. The comment says this allows joints to be outside of min and max values when starting.

The xacro sets PI to 3.14159265359 and the rotation-limit properties shoulder -3.05433 to 3.05433, arm -1.91986 to 0.640187, elbow -1.397485 to ${PI/2}, forearm -3.05433 to 3.05433, wrist -1.74533 to 1.91986, and hand -2.57436 to 2.57436.
joint_1 through joint_6 are revolute, and each limit lower and upper attribute names an xacro limit property.

joint_limits.yaml says joint properties can be changed with the keys max_position, min_position, max_velocity and max_acceleration, and the joint_1 entry sets max_velocity 2.2 and max_acceleration 1.5.
part_4.launch starts server_endpoint and the node sim_real_pnp running sim_real_pnp.py.
listener subscribes to topic sim_real_pnp with type MoverServiceRequest and callback plan_pick_and_place.
send_trajectory_goal sets RobotMoveGoal cmd.Trajectory and cmd.cmd_type to TRAJECTORY_COMMAND_ID, then calls send_goal and wait_for_result.
sim_real_pnp plan_pick_and_place waits for the action server niryo_one/commander/robot_action.
PICK_PLACE_HEIGHT_OFFSET is 0.065.
TrajectoryPlanner's serialized field m_RosServiceName defaults to niryo_moveit.
CurrentJointConfig copies each ArticulationBody jointPosition[0] into joints.joints.
PublishJoints builds a MoverServiceRequest from CurrentJointConfig and the target and placement poses converted with To<FLU>, and sends it to m_RosServiceName with TrajectoryResponse.
TrajectoryResponse starts ExecuteTrajectories when response.trajectories.Length is greater than 0.

ExecuteTrajectories writes each point's positions, multiplied by Mathf.Rad2Deg, as ArticulationBody xDrive targets, calls CloseGripper when poseIndex equals Poses.Grasp, and calls OpenGripper after the plans.
SourceDestinationPublisher's m_TopicName defaults to /niryo_joints, and Start registers a publisher of NiryoMoveitJointsMsg on that topic.
RealSimPickAndPlace's rosRobotCommandsTopicName defaults to niryo_one/commander/robot_action/goal.
RealSimPickAndPlace Start subscribes to rosRobotCommandsTopicName for RobotMoveActionGoal with ExecuteRobotCommands.
The pick-and-place Docker image starts FROM ros:melodic-ros-base.
The Docker image installs ros-melodic-moveit and ros-melodic-rosbridge-suite.
LICENSE.md says the software is made available under the Apache 2.0 license.
The niryo_moveit package.xml license element is Apache 2.0.
The ros_tcp_endpoint package version is 0.7.0 and its license element is Apache 2.0.

determinism.notes: The fake answers a fixed placeholder plan shape. A live MoveIt plan is not replayed.

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS recording fake of the niryo_moveit MoverService (no MoveIt, OMPL or Unity)
gaps: PLAN ONLY: the package never executes a plan
the fake's trajectories are placeholders and do not apply the callback's 0.05 m grasp drop
Unity executes trajectories only in the callback of its own request, so a receipt never shows motion of the simulated arm
the fake records the requested radian vector unchanged as the first plan's start and chains each later plan to the previous placeholder goal; it runs no IK, MoveIt, OMPL or collision checking

an empty trajectory list is a successful ROS response in the callback (mover.py:84-85 and the three later empty returns) and a failed receipt here, because the output contract requires four plans; a plan() that is false raises in plan_trajectory (mover.py:48-53) and is a failed call

the MoveGroupCommander is local (mover.py:75-76). rospy.spin only waits (mover.py:130) and does not serialise callbacks, so another /niryo_moveit client can overlap this one on the shared move_group. Plan only while Unity is not calling the service. Exclusive covers this endpoint's active calls only; a deadline or e-stop does not retire a plan already sent

joint travel for indexes 0, 1, 3, 4 and 5 is the xacro property pair. Elbow index 2 is operator_required because its upper is ${PI/2}. Pose components are operator_required. demo.launch allows 0.3 rad of start error past the URDF limits; this package does not add 0.3
the Unity arm and gripper, the ROS-TCP endpoint, the /niryo_joints publisher, and sim_real_pnp are NOT COVERED. niryo_one_ros is not cited
the operator runs rosbridge, which the tutorial image installs, next to part_3.launch. part_3.launch itself starts the ROS-TCP endpoint, not rosbridge

operator_required.name: plan_pick_and_place
operator_required.reason: elbow upper is the xacro expression ${PI/2}, which is not a cited number; the operator sets both ends

safe_state.description: Plan-only package: it sends nothing that executes a plan or commands the Unity arm, its gripper, or the Niryo action server. An e-stop latches this endpoint in software and refuses further planning requests. A request already sent is not awaited. There is no unpause. A pick-and-place that Unity started from its own button runs in Unity's coroutine and is not reached.
